author: IGN
description:
Marvel Studios tantalized fans by debuting a trailer (https://www.ign.com/articles/disney-debuts-new-avengers-doomsday-trailer-at-cinemacon-2026) for Avengers: Doomsday (https://www.ign.com/movies/avengers-doomsday) at CinemaCon back in April, but only for those lucky enough to be in the room where it happened. Fortunately, that trailer has now finally gone wide (https://www.ign.com/articles/first-proper-avengers-doomsday-trailer-reveals-thor-steve-rogers-and-doctor-doom-himself), and that means we’ve all gotten our first real taste of Robert Downey, Jr. as Doctor Doom. Suffice it to say, this isn’t just Iron Man in a green cape. 

The new Doomsday trailer doesn’t reveal a lot about the plot of the new film. If anything, it raises a bigger question about Doom’s role in this multiversal conflict. Is he the hero or the villain here? Is he the doomsday the Avengers and X-Men are desperate to prevent, or is he our heroes’ only hope against the coming destruction? Let’s take a closer look
title: Is Robert Downey Jr's Doctor Doom the Hero or Villain of Avengers: Doomsday?

author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Director Christopher Nolan's latest blockbuster is sailing past box office expectations with a $264 million dollar global opening weekend. This exceeds Nolan's previous record-holder, The Dark Knight Rises, which earned $249 million on opening weekend in 2012. The Odyssey cost nearly $400 million to produce and market, but it might not have to go on a odyssey of its own to recoup that money. In other news, Ryan Reynolds has ideas for Deadpool 4, and believes he's done doing solo Deadpool movies. After Deadpool & Wolverine made over $1 billion in theaters worldwide, Reynolds and Disney probably want to team him up with as many heroes as possible. And finally, we’re riding Mine Cart Madness inside Super Nintendo World with The Ride Guys at Universal Epic Universe at Universal Orlando Resort.
 
Presented by Universal Orlando Resort, and its newest theme park, Universal Epic Universe.
title: The Odyssey Sets New Record for a Christopher Nolan Film - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
Over the last 40-something years, there have been dozens of Spider-Man video games released across nearly every console and gaming platform imaginable. While a few of those have been genuine masterpieces, most aren’t great, but they all have their own unique charm and weird quirks: from Spider-Man Vs. The Kingpin’s fully voice-acted animated cutscenes and bizarre alternate endings to the deep-cut villains of the extremely rare 32X game Web of Fire to the fact that one of the first video game appearances of Spider-Man was as a boss fight in The Revenge of Shinobi where he turned into Batman. 

Join Max Scoville on a journey through some of the earliest days of Spidey’s gaming career, through several mountains of shovelware in the 8 and 16-bit eras, taking a look at how much this wall-crawler benefitted from the advent of 3D gaming. From the PS2-era tie-ins to Sam Raimi’s beloved film to Activision’s annualized releases that had to get creative without movies to gamify. Finally, the mod
title: A Long History of Games That Really Made Us Feel Like Spider-Man

Don't miss the 35th Anniversary Trailer for Point Break, the re-release of the action thriller distributed by Fathom Entertainment. Experience a classic once more restored in 4K in theaters with Point Break returning to theaters on August 16 and August 19.

In Los Angeles, a gang of bank robbers call themselves the Ex-Presidents and commit their crimes while wearing masks of Reagan, Carter, Nixon and Johnson. The FBI believes that the members of the gang could be surfers and sends young agent Johnny Utah undercover at the beach to mix with the surfers and gather information. As he is drawn deeper into the world of charismatic surfer Bodhi and his thrill-seeking crew, Utah must decide where his loyalties lie.

Point Break stars Patrick Swayze, Keanu Reeves, Gary Busey, Lori Petty, John C. McGinley, and more. The film is directed by Kathryn Bigelow and written by Rick King and W. Peter Iliff.

Point Break is returning to theaters on August 16 and August 19.
